focuses.title: The Constitution in Abeyance
focuses.description: The regime invokes the 1968 constitution while retaining exceptional powers. A functioning administration cannot settle the unresolved question of who may govern.

focuses.title: Entrench the Revolution
focuses.description: The officers retain the final political veto. Their command becomes firmer while the exclusion of civilian constituencies deepens.

focuses.title: Negotiate a Civilian Handover
focuses.requirements: A civilian transfer is being negotiated, or a civilian party already governs.
focuses.description: A transfer of authority requires guarantees to the services and a credible opening for the opposition. A negotiated departure avoids making another military conspiracy the foundation of civilian rule.

focuses.title: Retain the Exceptional Courts
focuses.description: Military jurisdiction protects the government from organized opposition. The same restrictions isolate universities and weaken the free circulation of expertise.

focuses.title: Political Amnesty and Open Courts
focuses.description: Political prisoners must be released and ordinary courts restored before parliamentary competition can be credible. The executive relinquishes instruments that made governing without consent easier.

focuses.title: A Free Parliamentary Mandate
focuses.requirements: Exceptional military rule has ended. Use the existing party and election system.
focuses.description: Legal political competition restores the distinction between a government and the state. The electorate chooses a cabinet through the existing parliamentary institutions rather than a prescribed successor.

focuses.title: A Parliamentary Republic
focuses.description: A free constitutional settlement removes the Crown as an independent center of executive authority. The change resolves one old division while alienating committed royalists.

focuses.title: A Crown Bound by Parliament
focuses.description: A freely accepted monarchy can offer continuity only if its powers are defined by parliament. Restraint on the government is the price of reconciling royalist institutions with elected authority.

focuses.title: The Development Programme
focuses.description: Public coordination has supported rapid expansion, but production and infrastructure remain unevenly distributed. The development programme must turn investment into a broader productive base.

focuses.title: Technical Schools and Returning Skills
focuses.description: Greece needs technicians at home as well as the remittances of workers abroad. Technical schools and recognition of returning workers skills reduce dependence on a narrow pool of specialists.

focuses.title: Credit for the Visitor Economy

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: Hotels, transport services and coastal businesses earn foreign exchange quickly. Directing scarce credit toward visitors leaves less capital for industrial diversification.

focuses.title: Credit for Industrial Investment

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: Manufacturing offers a broader export base and less seasonal employment. Its equipment and long construction schedules tie up credit that could otherwise serve commerce and tourism.

focuses.title: Island Transport and Services

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: Island communities need reliable links to the mainland before visitor spending can sustain local businesses. Maintaining those links remains a public obligation beyond the summer season.

focuses.title: Industrial Standards and Suppliers
focuses.description: Greek manufacturers must meet consistent standards and develop domestic suppliers. Better production discipline depends on continuing technical instruction.

focuses.title: Water and Rural Productivity

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: Irrigation, local roads and storage can connect agricultural districts to expanding urban markets. These works broaden the gains of growth without treating rural Greece as a reserve of departing labor.

focuses.title: Modernize the Cooperatives
focuses.description: Cooperative purchasing and processing give smaller farmers access to equipment and distribution. Public supervision also carries administrative costs and risks protecting inefficient organizations.

focuses.title: Competitive Farm Credit
focuses.description: Commercial credit rewards farms able to mechanize and sell at scale. The strongest producers gain quickly while smaller households face a harsher adjustment.

focuses.title: Piraeus and the Shipbuilding Base

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: A maritime country should retain more repair, engineering and construction work in its own ports. The shipbuilding base needs dependable public infrastructure as well as private orders.

focuses.title: Merchant Shipping Services
focuses.description: Shipping services bring earnings and expertise from a world-spanning Greek fleet. Dependence on international owners and foreign demand limits the state influence over those earnings.

focuses.title: A Domestic Marine Supply Chain

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: Domestic equipment and maintenance suppliers can keep more value in Greek yards. Building this network costs more than relying on established international suppliers.

focuses.title: A Joint Defence Staff
focuses.description: Political rivalries inside the services have damaged confidence in joint command. A professional planning staff can restore coordination while enlarging the permanent military administration.

focuses.title: Army Schools and Staff Courses
focuses.description: Training officers for combined operations matters more than multiplying political appointments. Staff education requires a continuing commitment to instructors and facilities.

focuses.title: An Aegean Command
focuses.description: The islands and sea lanes demand coordinated naval and air planning. A standing command gives that mission institutional weight and a recurring cost.

focuses.title: Depth Through Territorial Forces
focuses.description: Territorial formations provide a resilient framework for defending difficult ground. Their wider intake takes longer to train to a common standard.

focuses.title: Professional Cadres
focuses.description: A stronger professional cadre accelerates training and improves detailed preparation. Maintaining that cadre is more expensive than relying on a broad territorial establishment.

focuses.title: Sea Denial and Coastal Defence
focuses.description: Coastal defence and dispersed naval forces make hostile access to the Aegean costly. Concentration on denial leaves less capacity for expeditionary landings.

focuses.title: A Fleet for Sea Control
focuses.description: A fleet able to operate beyond the immediate coast can protect shipping and support distant forces. Its readiness and logistics consume a larger share of national resources.

focuses.title: Army Workshops and Maintenance

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: Repair capacity and domestic workshops reduce the distance between an equipment order and a field formation. Their value depends on sustained technical competence, not a political procurement announcement.

focuses.title: Air Defence of the Aegean
focuses.description: Control of the air is inseparable from the defence of islands and sea lanes. Air staffs must choose where a limited force can achieve the greatest effect.

focuses.title: Concentrate on Interception
focuses.description: Interceptor training and aircraft development prioritize the protection of national airspace. The supporting radar and technical establishment must be maintained continuously.

focuses.title: Concentrate on Battlefield Support
focuses.description: An air arm trained closely with land and naval forces can support a rapid operational decision. This approach accepts the continuing expense of specialized coordination.

focuses.title: Link the Radar Stations

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: Linked reporting stations make a scattered island defence less fragmented. Radar works must be placed where Greece actually controls the land and can maintain the equipment.

focuses.title: Recover Room for Diplomacy
focuses.description: Greece occupies an important strategic position but cannot assume that foreign governments will overlook its domestic settlement. Diplomatic room requires sustained attention and resources.

focuses.title: American Standardization
focuses.description: American facilities and equipment have long shaped the Greek defence establishment. A renewed agreement trades access and dependence for training, technical support and revenue.

focuses.title: A Diversified Defence Partnership
focuses.description: French procurement and training offer a second route to modern equipment. Diversification reduces reliance on one supplier while increasing the demands of technical support.

focuses.title: Negotiate Aegean Procedures
focuses.description: Working procedures at sea and in the air can reduce the risk of an accidental confrontation. Each government must accept restraints on how it demonstrates its claims.

focuses.title: Deterrence in the Aegean
focuses.description: Greece can invest in a more visible posture instead of a bilateral restraint agreement. Readiness carries economic costs and does not settle the underlying maritime disputes.

focuses.title: Restore European Association
focuses.requirements: Representative institutions, legal political competition and all current EC member governments approval.
focuses.description: The association signed in 1961 survived in restricted form after the coup, but its political and financial development stalled. Restoration requires a credible democratic settlement and agreement from the Community governments.

focuses.title: Apply for Community Membership
focuses.requirements: European association is active. Greece meets native membership conditions. Every current Community member consents.
focuses.description: Membership carries political obligations as well as economic opportunity. Greece applies through the existing Community institutions and accepts their adopted rules rather than declaring itself a member.

focuses.title: A Balkan Transit Understanding
focuses.description: Transit through Yugoslavia links Greek ports with markets beyond the northern frontier. Reliable infrastructure benefits both sides but requires each government to commit to practical cooperation.

focuses.title: A Northern Commercial Opening
focuses.description: The disappearance of Bulgarian territorial claims created space for more ordinary relations. Commercial cooperation can broaden trade without pretending that the two alliance systems have merged.

focuses.title: Coordinate with the British Guarantor
focuses.description: Britain remains a guarantor of Cyprus and holds sovereign base areas on the island. Coordination can strengthen crisis communications without granting Greece control of British forces or bases.

focuses.title: A German Technical Exchange
focuses.description: The labor relationship with West Germany can also support technical instruction and returning skills. A funded exchange gives both countries a concrete interest without scripting a population transfer.

focuses.title: The Officer Compact
focuses.description: The dictatorship rests on an officer coalition rather than an ordinary governing party. Preserving that coalition strengthens command but keeps the state dependent on military arbitration.

focuses.title: Papadopoulos and the Cabinet
focuses.description: Papadopoulos concentrates political authority around his cabinet and the development administration. Economic coordination offers a positive programme, while patronage makes that apparatus costly.

focuses.title: The Security Directorate

effects.text: An internal leadership change brings Ioannidis to actual power

focuses.requirements: The hardliners have secured control of the military government. This is an alternative leadership struggle, not the January 1970 starting leader.
focuses.description: Ioannidis and the security apparatus reject a civilian political opening. Their ascent must be a real change of leadership, with the diplomatic exposure that a harder dictatorship entails.

focuses.title: A Managed Political Opening
focuses.description: A controlled opening seeks expertise and international credibility without immediately surrendering the regime. Every concession also loosens the instruments of personal command.

focuses.title: Technocrats Under Military Tutelage

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: The cabinet can instead make development the substitute for political participation. Industrial expertise grows inside an administration whose military sponsors retain the final veto.

focuses.title: Promotion Through Loyalty
focuses.requirements: Dimitrios Ioannidis actually controls the government.
focuses.description: A loyal army command is less likely to challenge the security leadership. The price is renewed distrust from naval officers and other institutions excluded from promotion.

focuses.title: Bargain with the Services
focuses.requirements: Dimitrios Ioannidis actually controls the government.
focuses.description: An inter-service settlement gives naval professionalism room to recover. The army security network must accept that it cannot monopolize every appointment.

focuses.title: Civilian Ministries, Military Veto
focuses.description: Civilian specialists can administer complex programmes without holding sovereign political authority. Their inclusion makes the state more capable, not yet representative.

focuses.title: A Permanent Security Establishment
focuses.requirements: Dimitrios Ioannidis actually controls the government.
focuses.description: A permanent security establishment offers the leadership a stronger instrument for ambitious foreign policy. It also absorbs resources and increases the economic cost of political isolation.

focuses.title: An Order Beyond the Barracks
focuses.description: An enduring regime needs institutions able to outlast one circle of officers. Establishing predictable administration restrains arbitrary executive intervention even while elections remain absent.

focuses.title: A Civilian Conservative Mandate
focuses.description: The conservative tradition must prove that civilian authority can deliver stability without a military veto. Economic confidence and institutional credibility become the basis of its mandate.

focuses.title: Call Karamanlis Home

effects.text: Select Karamanlis through the existing Greek leader system

focuses.description: Karamanlis offers international standing and an established conservative constituency. His return also challenges politicians who kept the party tradition alive during exile.

focuses.title: The Kanellopoulos Tradition
focuses.description: A constitutional conservative leadership can build on Kanellopoulos and the pre-coup parliamentary tradition. Its reassuring continuity also leaves less room for a decisive break with older institutions.

focuses.title: Restore European Credit
focuses.description: European confidence rests on political credibility and concrete reforms. The conservative government prepares the economy for a negotiated relationship rather than treating admission as a unilateral right.

focuses.title: Constitutional Conservatism
focuses.description: Conservative authority is rooted in law, parliament and a disciplined administration. The same formal safeguards slow decisions that an authoritarian cabinet could simply impose.

focuses.title: Competitive Greek Enterprise

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: Competitive firms need productive investment rather than permanent protection from change. A stronger manufacturing base gives the civilian right a tangible economic programme.

focuses.title: Tax Compliance and Sound Accounts
focuses.description: Reliable tax collection strengthens public finances without relying on emergency levies. The bureaucracy needed to enforce the rules must itself be funded.

focuses.title: Credit for Productive Investment
focuses.description: Preferential credit can accelerate investment in productive firms. Its benefits arrive before the state recovers the revenue it has forgone.

focuses.title: Rebuild the Liberal Centre
focuses.description: The Centre Union tradition joins parliamentary legitimacy with administrative reform. Rebuilding that coalition requires institutions able to mediate its many constituencies.

focuses.title: A Professional Civil Service
focuses.description: Professional recruitment and reliable public records reduce the role of personal patronage. Ministers lose some discretion as expertise and procedure gain authority.

focuses.title: Parliament Before Palace
focuses.description: Parliamentary supremacy promises a clear answer to the conflicts of the 1960s. It also forces a confrontation with constituencies attached to an independent royal role.

focuses.title: A Broad Constitutional Compromise
focuses.description: A broad settlement can reassure the services and constitutional conservatives. Its breadth limits the freedom of the government that must uphold it.

focuses.title: Bring Development to the Provinces

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: Provincial infrastructure gives the parliamentary center a practical purpose beyond managing Athens. Better local connections make development visible outside the capital.

focuses.title: Free and Capable Universities
focuses.description: Universities require freedom to recruit and to argue, as well as dependable funding. Restoring that environment is an investment in expertise rather than a promise of immediate political obedience.

focuses.title: National Independence and Social Change
focuses.description: The Papandreou movement connects social reform with independence from external tutelage. Its programme deliberately challenges established owners and foreign partners.

focuses.title: A Social Contract
focuses.description: Labor and excluded constituencies must gain a legal voice if popular sovereignty is to be more than a slogan. A government that incorporates them also accepts new administrative obligations.

focuses.title: Public Control of Strategic Credit

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: Public control directs credit toward sectors the government considers strategic. It can expand industrial output while reducing private financial earnings and increasing administrative exposure.

focuses.title: A Negotiated Development Compact

guards: Native building cap and state capacity

focuses.description: A negotiated compact draws investment from private enterprise while securing public commitments. The state gains a wider economic coalition but accepts continued dependence on its partners.

focuses.title: A National Health Service
focuses.description: A national health service makes access to care a public responsibility rather than an accident of locality or income. The resulting security and productive gains require a larger recurring health budget.

focuses.title: Workers in Public Administration
focuses.description: Worker representation ties the administration to the social coalition that sustains the government. Consultation can improve policy acceptance while making administration more demanding.

focuses.title: An Independent Foreign Policy
focuses.description: A more independent policy reduces the influence of established patrons without assuming that alliance membership must vanish. Greater autonomy can restrict access to some external expertise.

focuses.title: Renegotiate the Western Bargain
focuses.description: The government can instead use its social mandate to seek better terms within the Western relationship. Access to capital and technology comes with continued external influence.

focuses.title: The Communist Left in Government
focuses.description: A legal communist government must translate an underground tradition into public institutions. Industrial planning and research take precedence over established commercial interests.

focuses.title: Rehabilitate Civil War Families
focuses.description: Rehabilitation addresses exclusions that outlasted the fighting itself. The settlement strengthens civic belonging while restricting the partisan use of the state.

focuses.title: An Orthodox Planning Line
focuses.description: A more orthodox line concentrates authority over industrial priorities. It delivers a stronger production programme at the expense of commercial flexibility.

focuses.title: A Broad Democratic Left Front
focuses.description: Cooperation with the non-orthodox left, including KKE Interior constituencies, broadens the political base. Pluralism brings expertise and legitimacy while limiting the governing party freedom of command.

focuses.title: Industrial Research Institutes
focuses.description: Applied research can connect the planned industrial base with sustained technical progress. Institutes need stable funding and genuine professional competence.

focuses.title: Eastern Industrial Terms
focuses.description: An industrial agreement with the Soviet Union offers another source of technical cooperation. The terms must be accepted by both governments and need not turn Greece into a subordinate state.

focuses.title: The Crown and the Nation
focuses.description: Royalists claim a source of legitimacy above ordinary party competition. That claim can rally supporters while reviving arguments over the Crown foreign connections.

focuses.title: A Constitutional Return for Constantine

effects.text: Confirm the King through the existing monarchist leader system

focuses.requirements: A freely accepted constitutional restoration, or a publicly mandated monarchist settlement.
focuses.description: The King return requires an agreed constitutional position, not a claim that the failed countercoup never happened. The invitation binds the restored institution to a public settlement.

focuses.title: A Crown under Parliament
focuses.description: A restrained monarchy can offer continuity without competing with the cabinet. The elected government gains confidence by accepting firm limits on executive discretion.

focuses.title: An Active Royal Executive
focuses.description: An active Crown offers a more decisive executive center. Reopening the question of royal intervention also revives the polarization that destabilized earlier parliamentary government.

focuses.title: Reconcile the Services
focuses.description: The royalist tradition is strongest in parts of the naval establishment but cannot substitute for inter-service confidence. Reconciliation requires professional representation and a funded command structure.

focuses.title: A Durable Constitutional Settlement
focuses.description: A durable settlement must make loyal opposition compatible with loyalty to the state. Patronage and public commitments are the cost of consolidating the restored institution.

focuses.title: Officers on Cyprus
focuses.requirements: Greece and Cyprus exist; an actual Greek officer footprint exists.
focuses.description: The Greek mission has institutional influence inside the Cypriot National Guard. Professional cooperation and political intervention are different uses of the same presence.

focuses.title: Honour the Republic
focuses.requirements: No war with Cyprus.
focuses.description: Respect for the Republic protects a cooperative Greek position without attempting to command Cypriot political life. Influence is exercised through accepted institutions rather than a clandestine veto.

focuses.title: The Officer Network
focuses.requirements: Greece is ruled by the actual military-junta party. Greek officer footprint remains. Once per campaign.
focuses.description: An officer network offers leverage over the government in Nicosia. Supporting it spends Greek political capital and creates a crisis which the other guarantors can answer.

focuses.title: A Guarantor Settlement

effects: Greece, Turkey and Britain receive Guarantor Consultations

focuses.requirements: An actual constitutional crisis exists.
focuses.description: The guarantors receive a real request for consultation. Neither Turkey nor Britain is assumed to agree with the Greek government merely because Athens completed a focus.

focuses.title: Withdraw the Network
focuses.requirements: The coup has not launched.
focuses.description: Withdrawing support for the clandestine network reduces Greek leverage but gives the Republic room to restore confidence. This choice is available before a coup attempt is launched.

focuses.title: Overthrow Makarios

effects: If successful: Sampson becomes the authored coup-government leader

focuses.requirements: Actual Greek junta remains in power. Officer penetration at least 60. Officer footprint exists. Cyprus remains independent and at peace with Greece. Once per campaign.
focuses.description: A coup can replace the Cypriot government if the officer network overcomes its prepared defence. Success creates a short strategic opening, not Greek ownership or a guaranteed victory over Turkey.

focuses.title: The Turkish Landing
focuses.requirements: An actual Turkey-Cyprus war from this crisis is active. Greece and Cyprus are independent. Greece is not already fighting Cyprus.
focuses.description: An actual Turkish-Cypriot war confronts Athens with a distinct choice. Limited aid and direct participation offer different benefits and dangers.

focuses.title: Volunteers for Cyprus

effects: Expense +0.002% of Greek GDP per week while the mission remains active
Cyprus Volunteer Mission (while the Cyprus mission remains eligible)

focuses.requirements: Turkey is at war with Cyprus. Greece is not at war with either country. Cyprus consents through the real volunteer diplomatic action. Native volunteer and diplomatic-action rules still apply.
focuses.description: A volunteer mission supports Cyprus while limiting the formal Greek commitment. It uses real Greek formations through native diplomacy and remains subject to engine deployment rules.

After related peace, Turkey: War support +2%

focuses.requirements: The Turkey-Cyprus war is active. Greece is not already at war with Turkey or Cyprus. Entry must place Greece alongside Cyprus. The temporary NATO exit and return are disclosed to both countries before entry.
focuses.description: Direct entry puts Greek forces on the Cypriot side against Turkey. Both prior NATO members leave before Greece joins, and return through the existing guarded process after both relevant wars end.

focuses.title: Civilian Cooperation with Cyprus
focuses.description: Civilian trade and technical cooperation give Greece an enduring stake in a stable Republic. Cyprus receives the actual terms and may accept or refuse them.

focuses.title: Prepare the Cypriot Officer Network
focuses.requirements: The Greek network and officer footprint are active. No coup has yet been launched.
focuses.description: A prepared network gives the coup a stronger chance than political sponsorship alone. The investment is sunk if Cypriot institutions contain it or Athens later withdraws support.

focuses.title: Exploit the Operational Initiative
focuses.requirements: The actual coup succeeded, the coup government remains in power in Cyprus, and the two countries are at peace. Once only.
focuses.description: A successful coup briefly gives the Greek command greater freedom to prepare its next move. The advantage expires, while diplomatic exposure and the cost of readiness make delay expensive.
focuses.weekly_lifetime: Only while the 180-day Operational Initiative spirit is active and the coup government still controls Cyprus.

focuses.title: An Agreed Guarantor Settlement
focuses.requirements: The Cypriot constitutional government is in office. Greece, Turkey, Britain and Cyprus must accept the security settlement.
focuses.description: A negotiated security settlement offers a durable alternative to a short military opening. It preserves Cypriot sovereignty and requires all four governments to accept their obligations.

starting_spirits.name: Emergency Rule
starting_spirits.description: Exceptional powers give the officer government administrative freedom while reducing political legitimacy and intellectual openness.
starting_spirits.remedy: Ends with an actual civilian handover; not merely a different cabinet label.

starting_spirits.name: Divided Officer Corps
starting_spirits.description: Personal loyalties and the failed royal countercoup divide the services. Neither navy professionalism nor army political power guarantees joint command.
starting_spirits.remedy: A Joint Defence Staff replaces the divided command arrangement.

starting_spirits.name: Suppressed Political Life
starting_spirits.description: Parties cannot compete freely, political detention continues and exceptional jurisdiction constrains public life. The formal easing of prior press censorship in late 1969 did not establish a free political system.
starting_spirits.remedy: Political Amnesty and Open Courts, or the enacted Social Contract under a real civilian mandate.

starting_spirits.name: Civil War Inheritance
starting_spirits.description: Exclusion, memories of the Civil War and conflicts over royal authority continue to divide public institutions.
starting_spirits.remedy: A freely accepted constitutional settlement or rehabilitation of excluded families.

starting_spirits.name: Uneven Development
starting_spirits.description: Rapid aggregate growth coexists with uneven regional infrastructure and less productive rural districts.

starting_spirits.name: Emigration and Technical Gaps
starting_spirits.description: Emigration brings remittances but makes technical capacity at home harder to maintain. This custom spirit imposes no workforce-size penalty.
starting_spirits.remedy: Technical Schools and Returning Skills, or Free and Capable Universities.

starting_spirits.name: Restricted European Association
starting_spirits.description: Association continues in limited treaty form, while further political integration and new Community financing are restricted. Greece is not a Community member in the historical January 1970 concept.
starting_spirits.remedy: Restore European Association through democratic reform and actual member-state approval.

starting_spirits.name: Maritime and Tourism Expansion
starting_spirits.description: Shipping, tourism and external earnings are real strengths of the economy. Their international exposure also limits economic autonomy.
starting_spirits.remedy: A continuing structural strength with a continuing external dependence.

starting_spirits.name: 1960 Treaty of Guarantee
starting_spirits.description: Cyprus, Greece, Turkey and the United Kingdom carry the existing treaty record. Consultation and the distinction from NATO remain explicit; it grants no automatic annexation or sovereign control.
starting_spirits.remedy: Retain the already installed four-country treaty spirit and crisis framework.
